text.p: Leg-spinner Paul
Strang followed his maiden test century on Friday with four for
58 to put Zimbabwe well on top on the second day of the first
test against Pakistan.
When bad light stopped play, the home side were 189 for six
in reply to Zimbabwe's 375 after an eventful day during which
spectators stoned their own side.
The fans, angered by Pakistan's failure to dismiss the
tourists in the first session, pelted their fielders with stones
and although no one was hurt lunch was taken five minutes early.
Zimbabwe, 240 for six overnight, reached their impressive
total through centuries from opener Grant Flower (110) and
Strang (106 not out), who carried their overnight partnership to
Flower, 98 overnight, hit the second century of his 19-test
career.
The tourists were bowled out in the third over after lunch
when promising debutant paceman Shahid Nazir rattled the stumps
of Henry Olonga to finish with five for 53 off 22.4 overs.
Strang, was dropped twice at 45 and 72, with paceman Waqar
Younis the unlucky bowler each time. He hit nine fours in a
206-ball innings that kept him at the crease for 325 minutes.
He also added a national record 87 for the ninth wicket with
brother Bryan who contributed a compact 42.
Aamir Sohail (46) and Saeed Anwar (51) gave Pakistan a
rousing start of 64 in 10.4 overs.
Sohail was in a belligerent mood, blasting 11 fours in his
run-a-ball knock, while Anwar struck six fours.
Anwar and Salim Malik, coming together at 91 for three,
added 51 for the fourth wicket before Strang broke the stand,
luring Anwar out of his crease to be stumped by Andy Flower.
After removing test newcomer Azam Khan for 14, Strang
claimed Malik as his fourth victim, bowling him round the legs
as he tried to sweep. Malik's 52 included six fours and a six
over long-on off Andrew Whittal.
Off-spinner Whittal disposed of Shadab Kabir for two, while
fast bowler Henry Olonga trapped Ijaz Ahmad lbw for nine.
At the close, Pakistani captain Wasim Akram was on five and
Moin Khan on three, with all the specialist batsmen back in the
pavilion and the initiative firmly with Zimbabwe.
